title: Why Do People Believe In Faith Healing?
summary: Josh and Chuck examine faith healing in two forms: intercessory prayer, which has been studied scientifically (including a coronary bypass prayer study where the prayed-for group that knew they were being prayed for fared worse), and the revival-style healing of evangelical and charismatic preachers. They cover the Pentecostal/charismatic roots in the 1906 Azusa Street Revival, the gift of healing, and the prosperity gospel. They describe revival-style performances and tricks such as earpieces, plants and catchers, profile Benny Hinn, Peter Popoff (exposed by James Randy on the Carson show), Hobart Freeman (who died refusing medical care), Catherine Coleman, and Aimee Semple McPherson. They discuss psychic surgery (with Andy Kaufman's Philippines trip), spontaneous remission and the placebo effect, the harms of faith healing, and child-neglect religious exemptions in Idaho and other states, including the 1974 federal Child Abuse Prevention and Treatment Act. The episode closes with a listener mail about a teacher using the Harriet Tubman episode in class, and a tangent on Bob Tilton and Adult Swim.
topics: Child Abuse Prevention and Treatment Act

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with long off-topic banter about Bon Jovi, Thompson Twins and concerts before moving to faith healing.

segments.title: Two kinds of faith healing and intercessory prayer
segments.summary: They distinguish prayer-based faith healing from evangelical hands-on healing and describe the scientific difficulty of studying intercessory prayer, including the sharpshooter effect.

segments.title: Coronary bypass prayer study
segments.summary: A study of prayer for bypass patients at six hospitals found the group that knew it was being prayed for fared worse than the unprayed group.

segments.title: Faith healers on stage and Catherine Coleman
segments.summary: Evangelical faith healers are described, along with Catherine Coleman, a 1960s-70s healer whose 1967 case study found none of 23 supposedly healed people were actually healed, including a woman whose spine collapsed.

segments.title: Charismatic Christianity and Pentecostal origins
segments.summary: The hosts trace evangelical, charismatic and Pentecostal Christianity to the 1906 Azusa Street Revival, explain gifts of knowledge, tongues and healing, and the split with traditional Christianity.

segments.title: Benny Hinn revival and staging
segments.summary: Describes the multi-day Benny Hinn revival, holy laughter, catchers, and tricks such as earpieces and planted audience members.

segments.title: Peter Popoff, Hobart Freeman and types of healers
segments.summary: Three types of healers are contrasted: Benny Hinn, Peter Popoff, whose earpiece fraud was exposed by James Randy on the Carson show, and Hobart Freeman, who died refusing medical care; the hosts also discuss Aimee Semple McPherson's stage shows.

segments.title: Psychic surgery and Andy Kaufman
segments.summary: Psychic surgery is explained as sleight of hand with chicken gizzards and blood packets; Andy Kaufman's trip to the Philippines is discussed.

segments.title: Spontaneous remission, placebo effect and harms
segments.summary: Skeptical explanations are covered: spontaneous remission of cancer, the placebo effect and anxiety, plus the harms of avoiding medical care and losing money.

segments.title: Religious exemptions and child medical neglect
segments.summary: Religious exemptions from child neglect laws are discussed, especially Idaho's record with Peaceful Valley Cemetery and the 1974 federal Child Abuse Prevention and Treatment Act interpretation later rescinded.
topics: Child Abuse Prevention and Treatment Act

segments.title: Bob Tilton and closing tangents
segments.summary: The hosts discuss televangelist Bob Tilton's prosperity show and fart compilations, then tangent to Adult Swim dubbed laugh tracks.

segments.title: Listener mail: teacher using Harriet Tubman episode
segments.summary: A listener who is an eighth-grade English teacher says his class used the Harriet Tubman episode in lessons.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts give social media and email contact details and sign off.
